subject: SSO session provenance & emergency access reconciliation
messages:
From: Kara Nguyen <kara@springwell.io>
To: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
Cc: Ravi Patel <ravi@healthfront.com>
Date: Fri, 09 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: SSO session provenance + emergency access logs

Hi Mina,

As part of our SIG review for Springwell Health (attestation window Apr 1–Apr 30), the security team asked for a sample of SSO assertion payloads and a reconciliation of emergency/on-call access events for that month. They want evidence showing: which accounts used emergency elevation, who approved them, and corresponding SSO assertion context (IDP attributes, session start/stop).

Can Redwood provide: 1) a redacted sample of assertion dumps (10–20 assertions), 2) a SCIM delta for April capturing provisioning/deprovisioning events tied to those accounts, and 3) an emergency access log (audit entries) that links to approval records? If possible, we need the artifacts by EOD Tuesday (May 12) so our compliance ops can include them in the SIG packet.

Appreciate it — let me know if a different format is preferred.

Thanks,
Kara Nguyen
Senior Security Analyst
Springwell Health
[Attachment: request-checklist.pdf (PDF, 120KB)]

From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
To: Kara Nguyen <kara@springwell.io>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 09 May 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: SSO session provenance + emergency access logs

Kara — thanks for the clear ask. We can produce the three artifacts you listed. Quick clarifications to make sure the package maps cleanly to your SIG fields:

- Assertion samples: we will redact PII (emails replaced with user IDs) and strip any full IP addresses; do you need full raw SAML XML, or would a mapped key/value extraction (nameID, sessionIndex, attributes) be preferable?
- SCIM delta: we can export the April delta CSV with audit timestamps and action type (create/patch/delete). Note: SCIM IDs are internal UUIDs; we will include a mapping file for any human-readable usernames.
- Emergency access: we maintain a gated JIT approval workflow (policy: on-call escalation) and a separate admin approval log. We can include the approval record IDs and a small CSV linking approval_id -> approver -> target_account -> timestamp. Full event logs (kept in compressed archive) can be provided as well.

Attachments we plan to include:
- scim_delta_2026-04.csv (CSV, ~45KB)
- sso_assertions_sample.txt (10 assertions, redacted)
- emergency_access_log_2026-04.zip (audit entries + approval mapping, encrypted stub)

Target: we can deliver the bundle by EOD May 12. Could you confirm whether the security team needs the raw SAML XML? If so we'll include it as an optional file (raw_saml_samples_2026-04.xml).

I'll loop Jonas to handle the assertion extraction and Sean to pull the JIT approval mapping.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Security Engineer | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: internal-checklist.md (TXT, 4KB)]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>, Kara Nguyen <kara@springwell.io>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: SSO session provenance + emergency access logs

On Fri, May 9, 2026 at 10:03 AM Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com> wrote:
> Kara — thanks for the clear ask. We can produce the three artifacts you listed.

Kara — quick note on the assertion sample format. For SIG reviewers it’s usually easier to consume parsed attributes (email hash, groups, authnInstant, sessionIndex) in a TSV. I've exported 10 redacted assertions and a mapping file that preserves the sessionIndex -> user_id relationship.

I attached the sample extract and the SCIM delta slice for the exact date ranges referenced. The emergency access mapping required a small correlation step against the incident bridge IDs — I included that as approval_mapping.csv.

Attachments included in this message: [scim_delta_2026-04.csv (CSV, 45KB)], [sso_assertions_sample.txt (TXT, 8KB)], [approval_mapping.csv (CSV, 6KB)]

If Springwell needs the full compressed audit set for log ingestion, Mina and I can hand off an encrypted archive through the secure drive link Mina will share.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Applied Security Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Kara Nguyen <kara@springwell.io>

- scim_delta_2026-04.csv (CSV) — user lifecycle events for Apr 1–30, includes external_id mapping column
- sso_assertions_sample.txt (TXT) — 10 redacted assertions (parsed attribute view)
- emergency_access_log_2026-04.zip (ZIP, encrypted) — event records + approval_mapping.csv

Shared link (secure): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b-ssosamples (access granted to springwell-security@springwell.io)

Sean Gallagher
